sources.quote: page no longer displays ZIP files, which previously allowed users to download large batches of compressed documents at once.
sources.searcher_note: Same finding: zip links on the DOJ Disclosures page gone as of Feb. 6, per a Jan. 30 Wayback capture. Says Jan. 30 capture had zip links for Data Sets 1-8 and 11, while 9 and 10 showed 'View files'. DOJ did not respond; SPJ quoted.

sources.searcher_note: Primary record: a court-case page now titled '[redacted] v. Epstein'. Confirms the renamed titles exist but shows no change date. Sibling pages for 9:10-cv-81111 and 9:09-cv-81092 carry the same form.

sources.quote: The Department of Justice removed 47,635 files from the publicly available database of Jeffrey Epstein case files, including various claims against President Donald Trump.
sources.searcher_note: Related Epstein Library removals; DOJ says files come back after redactions for victim concerns. Bears on the privacy-cleanup explanation; no mention of zip links or case-title renames.

notes: Zip-link removal is reported by Discrepancy Report (2026-02-11), which names the Epstein Library and dates it from the same Jan. 30 Wayback capture. It counts 9 data sets with zip links on Jan. 30 (1-8 and 11), not 11 of 11 as the lead says. No source found reporting the 2026-02-21/24 renaming of court-case links to '[redacted] v. ...'; DOJ's own pages show the renamed titles with no date. The DOJ Disclosures page fetched 2026-09-25 shows Data Sets 1-12 and no 'Download all files (zip)' links, but its text gave no quotable sentence, so it is not recorded. No coverage dated after 2026-06-30 on the zip links found. justice.gov/epstein/court-records returned HTTP 403.
